edges.description: Degeneration of the language network is what produces the progressive, initially isolated loss of language function that defines the syndrome; the isolation of the deficit is what distinguishes it from the other frontotemporal dementia syndromes at onset.

Behavioural involvement is a later consequence of the same degenerative process rather than a parallel one: the diagnostic criteria require language to remain isolated for at least two years, and behaviour is named among the domains the disease progresses into. The edge is marked indirect because the entry does not model that spread as a node of its own.
intermediate_mechanisms: Degeneration spreads beyond the language network as the disease progresses, recruiting behaviour, executive function and judgment.

evidence.reference_title: A review on primary progressive aphasia.
evidence.snippet: Primary progressive aphasia (PPA) is a neurodegenerative disease of insidious onset presenting with progressive isolated loss of language function, without significant impairment in other cognitive domains.

evidence.reference_title: A review on primary progressive aphasia.
evidence.snippet: Current diagnostic criteria require the language dysfunction to remain isolated for at least two years, and to remain the salient feature as the disease progresses, usually to involve other domains such as behavior, executive functions, and judgment.

nodes.description: Neurodegenerative processes selectively affect language networks, leading to progressive loss of language function with initial sparing of other domains.
